‹ Routine eye care

UV protection and sunglasses

The sun's ultraviolet (UV) rays can harm your eyes just like they harm your skin, and the damage adds up over a lifetime.

Years of UV exposure are linked to:

  • Cataracts
  • Growths on the surface of the eye (pinguecula and pterygium)
  • Skin cancers on and around the eyelids

Short, intense exposure can even sunburn the front of the eye (photokeratitis), which can occur after intense UV exposure, particularly around water or snow.

How sunglasses protect your eyes

Look for lenses that block 100% of UVA and UVB rays (often labeled "UV400"). Darker lenses don't automatically block more UV. Larger or wraparound frames keep out more light from the sides, and a wide-brimmed hat adds even more protection. UV reaches your eyes on cloudy days too, and water, sand and snow reflect it back at you. A comprehensive eye exam checks the health of your eyes.

Protect kids' eyes, too

Children spend a lot of time outdoors, and children's eyes are especially vulnerable to UV exposure. Sunglasses and a hat are a good habit to start early.
